chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a group of people for whom the sacrificial animals were too expensive, and they were performing Tamattu', and they were traveling companions, and they were not of one family, and they had gathered in their journey and their tent was one. Is it for them that they should slaughter one cow? He said: I do not like that unless it is from necessity.

key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعُونَ: Performing Tamattu' Hajj (combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: Can a group of unrelated travelers share one cow for Hajj sacrifice?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while a single cow can suffice for multiple unrelated travelers performing Tamattu' Hajj, it is merely permissible (ja'iz) rather than preferred (afdal), reserving the ideal practice for individual or family units. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic distinction between the validity of the sacrifice and its spiritual merit, emphasizing that sharing a cow among strangers lacks the communal warmth associated with the Prophet's household. The condition of 'necessity' (darurah) typically refers to financial constraints, allowing the group to pool resources without invalidating the ritual obligation.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I asked Abu Ibrahimasws (7th Imamasws about a group of people who found the sacrificial animal as too expensive, and they were performing Tumatto, and they were friends and were not of one family, and they had gathered during their journey, and their tent was one. Is it for them that they should be slaughtering one cow?’ So heasws said: ‘Iasws do not like that unless it is from a necessity’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a people for whom offering animals become very expensive, who are for al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous), in one company but not of the same family. They have come together; their way and camp is one, if they can slaughter one cow. He (the Imam) said, ‘I do not like it unless it is urgency.’”
